.]] Engineering is a primary crafting profession that can create many useful, unique and amazing items, as well as junk (but often explosive junk!). Engineers can create helpful items for generally all classes to be used in PvE or PvP. To counterbalance this usefulness, most items crafted by engineering require engineering skill to use, and many of these items come with a chance for unexpected backfires with often hilarious results. Hunters in particular see much use for engineered guns and scopes. Engineering profession recipes are known as schematics. Some notable engineer-crafted items are: * Jeeves, providing repair services to everyone and bank access to the engineer. * MOLL-E, allowing

An enemy, for the purpose of combat targeting, is: # Any mob (or their pet) with which you have less than friendly faction reputation (neutral, unfriendly, hostile and hated). # A PvP flagged player (or their pet) of the opposite faction. # Any player (or their pet) you are currently dueling. # Critters. Those poor squirrels. Note that it is possible, through reputation changes, for friendly NPCs to become ememies and vice versa. More generally, "enemy" may refer to the faction opposite the player's own (e.g. Horde for a night elf), or any faction opposed to the player's, regardless of attackable status.

.]] Engineers are practitioners of engineering. They are of many Azeroth's races and are affiliated with various factions. There are also siege engineers. Superior engineers are called chief engineers. Under the guidance of uncooperative mo'arg engineers, demon hunters were able to create several portals to Mardum. In WoW, they act as vendors or trainers.
An engineering trainer is an NPC that offers engineers the opportunity to train and learn recipes.

Engineering recipes, called schematics, are used by engineers to create item enhancements, explosives, goggles, toys, trinkets, guns and bows, fireworks, tools, and mounts. Many schematics are taught by Engineering trainers, while other schematics may be purchased from a vendor, obtained as loot, or given as a reward for completing an Engineering quest. The acquisition of some schematics requires a level of reputation with certain factions, which can be viewed in the Engineering faction recipes table.

This is a guide to finding and utilizing the Engineering Suppliers scattered throughout Azeroth. In many cases these vendor NPCs can sell you those quest and material Engineering items that would otherwise take you a few hours to grind. It's not a bad idea to make the rounds and stock up on a few of these supplies just in case. Prolific materials, such as Rough and Coarse Blasting Powders, are omitted in favor of the more esoteric necessities.

The Endmire is a large marshland located in between the Castle, Ceremony, Village, and Catacombs Wards—across eastern Revendreth. A small section can also be found in the Forest Ward, and another in the Catacombs Ward. It is a place with a different blend of strange, an unnerving warped reality composed of creatures that defy sense and explanation, with a wide assortment of aberrations and colors flitting about in an unchecked bog. Under normal circumstances, the stoneborn would keep these manifestations under control, but now they are simply tossing these strange creatures down. The Dredgers also keep the [https://wowhead.com/spell=304510/endmire effects] of the mire at bay through anima-fu

Enhancer is a rarely used catch-all term for consumable items that enhance (buff, enchant, etc.) other items either permanently or temporarily, but are not food, drink or poisons. Enhancers generally fall into two categories: augments and imbues. Augments are permanent attributes added to an item. An augment placed on an item that already has one (of any other type) will replace the old one. (An "are you sure" dialog appears if the augment is being placed via an item.) Imbues are temporary attributes added to an item. As with augments, a new imbue will push out an old one. An item can have both an augment and an imbue at the same time. ;Examples of enhancers: *Arcana augment *Armor Kits augm

Enohar Thunderbrew is a dwarf quest giver found in Nethergarde Keep in the Blasted Lands. Before she was a brewer, she was a hunter and is experienced with using bows. She loves Nethergarde Bitter beer, which she seems to be constantly drinking. She survives the assault of the Ironmarch and is found in a small camp with Maraad and Commander Vines. At her orders, the Dreadmaul ogres were poisoned as they had attacked with the orcs on Nethergarde and her sister died.

The Enraged Panther is a panther found in a cage in the Thousand Needles. Wizlo Bearingshiner's caravan was transporting the panther until it was attacked by centaurs. Wizlo has the Panther Cage Key, but had left a gizmo tied around the panther's neck. Respawn time is at least 15 minutes.
